brief: My balcony is full sun with moderate moisture, and a cat and a dog live in the household. A sunny balcony and one cat. I would like some cat grass for her to nibble on.

design.site_summary: A full sun balcony with moderate moisture, shared with one cat and one dog.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme is structured with hanging trailing plants on the upper railing, upright structural shrubs and perennials at mid height against the back wall, and a dedicated low floor-level tray for the pet accessible grazing zone.
design.combination_logic: The combination relies on contrasting fine grassy textures of the cat grass with the bold, architectural foliage of ornamental grasses and flowering perennials. Throughout the year, the scheme shifts from spring green shoots to summer blooms and textural autumn seed heads.

zones.placement: On the exterior side of the sunny railing, receiving 6 or more hours of direct midday sun.

plants.why: Thrives in full sun, trails gracefully over the railing edge, and is completely non-toxic to pets.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides a cascade of star-shaped blue flowers that soften the hard lines of the metal railing and contrast with upright plants.

maintenance: Water daily during peak summer heat as hanging pots dry out quickly.
Feed with a balanced liquid fertilizer every two weeks in spring and summer.
Trim back spent flower stems in mid-summer to encourage a second flush of blooms.

zones.placement: In large containers against the back wall, receiving full sun all afternoon.

plants.why: Loves full sun, tolerates drought, and provides an evergreen vertical element that is pet safe.
plants.role_in_combination: Contributes woody texture, aromatic scent, and a contrasting evergreen color against the seasonal flowers.

plants.why: A resilient sun-lover that provides great vertical height and striking summer blooms.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds bright pink color and coarse floral texture that stands tall behind the cascading and grazing layers.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top two inches of soil feel dry.
Feed once in early spring with a slow-release organic fertilizer.
Prune rosemary lightly after flowering to maintain shape; cut back coneflower stems in late winter.

zones.placement: In a heavy, stable low wooden planter directly on the balcony floor, easily reached by the cat in full sun.

plants.why: Fast-growing, highly palatable grass specifically planted for the cat to safely nibble.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides fine, soft vertical blades that contrast sharply with the broader leaves and woody stems of the mid-level plants.

maintenance: Keep the soil evenly moist but not waterlogged.
Resow fresh seed trays every 4 to 6 weeks as the grass gets chewed down or exhausted.
No chemical fertilizers should be used in this food-contact zone.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture in all containers and water deeply until it runs out the drainage holes.
care_instructions.frequency: Daily in summer, twice a week in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Apply organic liquid fertilizer to mid-level containers and hanging baskets to sustain heavy summer flowering.
Inspect plants for common balcony pests like aphids and rinse foliage with a gentle stream of water.

care_cautions: Hanging baskets on the railing can dry out extremely fast in full summer sun, leading to leaf drop on the Campanula.
The cat grass tray on the floor may get waterlogged if drainage holes clog, leading to root rot in the damp soil.
Dogs might be tempted to dig in the low grazing box, so the planter needs to be heavy and stable enough not to tip over.
design.pet_safety_note: All selected plants (Trailing Bellflower, Creeping Rosemary, Coneflower, and Cat Grass) are entirely non-toxic to cats and dogs, ensuring a safe environment for your pets to share.
